text: OVERDOSAGE Reactions due to overdosage are generally systemic in nature and involve the central nervous system and the cardiovascular system. See ADVERSE REACTIONS . Should convulsions or signs of respiratory depression and arrest develop, the patency of the airway and adequacy of ventilation must be assured immediately. See MANAGEMENT OF ADVERSE REACTIONS . The approximate oral LD50 of lidocaine hydrochloride in mice is 520 mg/kg. Plasma levels in excess of 8 mcg/mL in humans have been associated with serious adverse effects. Dialysis is of negligible value in the treatment of acute overdosage from lidocaine hydrochloride.
